It's really hard to keep this list short, but I'll try...

Nina Simone - Black Gold (RCA LSP-4248) [1970]
Some great live recordings on here, Nina was always such a compelling performer. Also heard on this record is Juma Sultan on congos, who also played at Woodstock.

King Tubby's "Controls" (feat. Aggrovators) (Clocktower Records 8802) [1990]
The first reggae album I bought, I could still play this any day of the week end to end. Timeless dub from the master.

Jake Slazenger - Nautilus (Warp Records WAP 75) [1996]
This little gem is a side project of Mike Paradinas (µ-Ziq). If you'e into the old Warp catalog this is a real nice find.

Botchit Breaks 4 - (Botchit and Scarper) [2001]
Honestly my DnB/breakbeat collection is pretty weak but this is the best album in it and the first set of records I bought. Solid mixable beats from an era of sound that's mostly been overshadowed this decade.

El-P Presents: Cannibal Oxtrumentals (Def Jux DJX24) [2001]
The most hauntingly beautiful, grimy New York hip-hop. Like newspapers blowing down gutters on a windy fall day. Cannibal Ox rocked these beats well, but there's no distracting from El-P's incredible production here. Must listen to album for hip-hop heads.

Squarepusher Ultravisitor promo single (Warp Records WARPLP117S) [2003]
Another Warp rarity I scored back when I was more active in collecting and following music scenes. Ultravisitor was a bit of a hit and miss album, but the hits were admittedly pretty amazing. Included on this 3 track promo record is the track "Square Window", not released anywhere else, to my knowledge. It is one of the best Squarepusher tracks of all time, especially if you have the vinyl because it sounds so good slowed down.

Of course I have more, but those are some of my favorites that are a bit unique.
